reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and stood around 5 feet 2 inches tall is a widespread historical myth. At his death, Napoleon was recorded as measuring 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French units (pieds and pouces). Because French inches were longer than British inches (each French inch being about 2.71 cm compared to the British inch of 2.54 cm), his actual height was approximately 5 feet 6 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (roughly 168–170 cm). For an early 19th-century French male, this was average or even slightly above average height. The enduring perception of him being miniature stems from unit conversion confusion and British wartime propaganda (such as caricatures by James Gillray).
